text:
Ana: Heads up — noticed p99 tail regressions on streaming chat after the mb_size bump to 8 on the A100 pools.
Raj: saw that in dashboards, p95 looks fine but p99 jumped. any traces?
Matt: I pulled a few flamegraphs. interestingly, many tails show fallback to the generic kernel at the end of generation.
Sasha: is that the kernel selector switching because of KV cache misses / sequence length variance?
Ana: exactly. when we increase mb_size we get better throughput, but streaming steady-state relies on very high KV hit ratio. rb: hit-rate dropped to ~64% on streaming traces vs ~92% for non-streaming completions.
Raj: numbers? can you paste the perf snippet?
Ana: here — from perf-batcher logs during a 10m window (mb_size=8):

```
batcher: mb_size=8 window=10m processed=1.2M tokens
kv-cache: hit_rate=0.64 miss_rate=0.36
kernel: selected=opt-aml-v2 fallback=generic-slow count_fallbacks=1.9k
latencies: p50=45ms p95=118ms p99=412ms
```

Matt: compare with non-streaming completions (mb_size=8):

```
batcher: mb_size=8 processed=900k tokens
kv-cache: hit_rate=0.91 miss_rate=0.09
kernel: selected=opt-aml-v2 fallback=generic-slow count_fallbacks=120
latencies: p50=38ms p95=82ms p99=180ms
```

Sasha: so streaming is causing more KV churn -> more fallback -> big p99. makes sense: streaming interleaves many short-turn requests and partial prefixes, so prefix reuse is lower.
Raj: any mitigation ideas? reduce mb_size for streaming only? change kernel-selection heuristic to prefer opt kernel even on some misses? prefetch KV? cache warming?
Ana: quick experiments I ran:
- Strategy A: mb_size=4 for streaming pools => p99 dropped to 190ms, throughput -18%.
- Strategy B: keep mb_size=8 but change selector to prefer opt-aml-v2 unless 8+ consecutive miss events => p99 ~245ms, throughput unchanged, some correctness risk.
- Strategy C: add small per-session warmup (single-request prefetch) before streaming burst => p99 170ms, throughput -6%.

Matt: Strategy C sounds promising. can you share the warmup patch diff?
Ana: snippet:

```
# runtime config
streaming_warmup.enabled=true
streaming_warmup.max_prefetch=1
streaming_warmup.timeout_ms=50
```

Raj: how did you measure correctness/race conditions? any observed hallucination or token divergence?
Ana: ran 5k synthetic sessions, automated eval on reference prompts — no measurable delta in output quality (BLEU/EMB sim within noise). so far safe.
perf-bot: alert: increased memory churn observed with warmup on small instances (+4% RSS)
Sasha: small but ok if it fixes tails. what about fallback count? did it drop?
Ana: fallback count dropped ~85% after warmup on our sample window.
Matt: can we A/B the warmup on a small % of traffic? get business metric impact and regression alerts.
Raj: yes. I'll wire up a canary rollout: 5% streaming traffic to warmup, monitor p99, throughput, and cost.
Ana: created experiment: `exp/stream-warmup-v1` — config attached to canary pool. Start when infra approves.
Sasha: infra-bot, grant canary pool creation for raj?
infra-bot: request received. ETA 20m to provision pool.
Raj: thanks — I'll prepare dashboards (p50/p95/p99, KV hit-rate, fallback count, tokens/sec) and smoke tests.
Ana: follow-up tasks:
- Raj: create canary and dashboards (ETA today EOD)
- Matt: add a debug metric to kernel-selector to surface decision reasons (ETA 2d)
- Sasha: run scale test with mix of short/long streaming sessions (ETA tomorrow)
- Ana: collect 24h traces, compare strategy A/B/C and post results in this thread (ETA 48h)

Matt: one more thought — we should update batching heuristics to prefer smaller mb_size for routes flagged as low prefix-reuse (chatty sessions).
Raj: Agreed. For now canary warmup + kernel debug metrics will give us answers.
Ana: thanks all. keeping this thread as the single source for the experiment.
Sasha: :thumbsup:
perf-bot: experiment created: id=exp-stream-warmup-v1 canary=5% monitor=p99,p95,kvcache,fallbacks
